# #486 written plan — revision 03 · 2/5 · boundaries.md

# Execution-boundary decisions · revision 03

Anchors are repository-relative on signed main `02351e2`. In the table, bare handler filenames live under `packages/engine/src/handlers/`. **T** = `TEMPLATE_ERROR`, **E** = `EXPRESSION_ERROR`, **M** = `MUTATION_ERROR`. Each such entry uses the safe cause construction and fixed boundary label in the plan, the current node as the failure owner, and **Resume false** unless the row explicitly gives an existing exception. Human ordinals are one-based in messages, indices zero-based in details. Higher-priority interruptions retain their existing policy.

**JSONata qualification for this matrix.** B05, B07–B08, B10–B14, B19 and B22 cover expressions or predicates, including the expression arms of inference mutations. The E or M in those rows applies to the eligible data-only authored site and the same-call evaluator observation. Public causes use fixed field/direction text even for direct literal `$error`. A missing specific cause takes the fixed evaluation fallback at an eligible site. A preparation, coercion, conversion or external failure with no qualifying evaluation observation keeps its existing site handling. Check custom-patch result shape/region separately after evaluation. B20, B25, P01/P02 and A01–A04 retain their contracts. [Execution and predicate boundary](expression-provenance.md)

| ID and site | Public code, boundary and bounded reason | Node, effect and recovery evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B01 · script.ts:15–62 | T · `script.args`, argument index and Liquid reason | Script. Check historical unfinished dispatch first. Current workspace/secret reads may have happened. Zero new dispatch marker and zero runner calls. No `script` evidence invented. Earlier unresolved effect retains consent-based uncertainty. |
| B02 · heartbeat.ts:18–20 | T · `heartbeat.probe.headers`, own-key iteration ordinal and Liquid reason | Heartbeat. Earlier beats may exist. Zero current fetch and no new beat. |
| B03 · heartbeat.ts:21–43 | T · `heartbeat.probe.url` or `heartbeat.probe.body`, Liquid reason | Heartbeat. Render ordered URL/body before calling fetch. HTTP rejection, overflow and response conversion have their own paths. |
| B04 · heartbeat.ts:49–81 | T · `heartbeat.probe.args`, argument index | Heartbeat. No new workspace resolution/runner/beat after argument failure. Heartbeat uses its existing probe semantics, independent of ordinary script dispatch consent. |
| B05 · heartbeat.ts:129–150 | E · `heartbeat.until`, predicate reason and beat number | Heartbeat. Probe already ran, and beat append completed. Keep its existing full/summary event and exactly one observed beat; failure cannot schedule another probe or timer. |
| B06 · heartbeat.ts:151–175 | T · `heartbeat.deadline`, Liquid reason or fixed “deadline must render to a timestamp” | Heartbeat. Same post-beat effects. Existing typed NaN branch currently echoes the rendered value and defaults to resumable. Align this branch to false and fixed safe cause. Successful until bypasses deadline. |
| B07 · subloop.ts:53–55, common.ts:108–139 | E · `subloop.input.messages.where` or `subloop.input.artifacts.where`, item index and predicate reason | Parent subloop. After existing-child guard, before new child. Built-in selection modes do no evaluation. |
| B08 · subloop.ts:58–64 | E · `subloop.input.vars`, own-key iteration ordinal and expression reason | Parent subloop, no child created. Conversion of the evaluated value with `toJson` remains separate. |
| B09 · subloop.ts:66–74 | T · `subloop.input.inject.content`, message index | Parent subloop. Render before message ID/clock callbacks. No child created. |
| B10 · subloop.ts:219–233 | E · `subloop.input.trigger.payload`, expression reason | Parent subloop. Before atomic child start. Serializer and child-start/storage errors keep their provenance. |
| B11 · subloop.ts:98–124,238–326 | E · `subloop.output.custom.patch`, evaluation reason; fixed “result is not a JSON patch” or “patch writes outside the mutable regions” for the recognized result checks | Parent subloop. Child terminal; completion bundled with failure. Normalize deterministic shape/region branches to false. Restrict the mutable-region catch to the known domain failure. Final executor commit still owns patch/thread errors. No child-failure link keys in parent mapping details. |
| B12 · subloop.ts:134–146,301–325 | E · `subloop.output.vars`, own-key iteration ordinal and expression reason | Parent subloop, after child, before parent commit. One child and one observed completion for the terminal sequence. Mapping failure carries no child-failure link keys. |
| B13 · subloop.ts:148–160,301–325; common.ts:108–139 | E · `subloop.output.messages.where` or `subloop.output.artifacts.where`, item index and predicate reason | Parent subloop; same completion and attribution as B12. No fabricated failed-child provenance when a successful child is being mapped. |
| B14 · inference.ts:295–310, common.ts:225–311, domain mutations.ts:80–121,166–330 | M · `inference.input`, operation index/kind, safe cause from the new inference mapper at the existing operation hooks | Inference. Transient view. Earlier structured coerce may have run. No new main turn on this failure. On eligible re-entry retain prior provenance. Provider refusals/timeouts and final serializers retain their own paths. |
| B15 · inference.ts:311–317 | T · `inference.contextFiles.template`, file index, Liquid reason, number of earlier successful writes if reported | Inference. Preserve ordered render/write. Zero writes of failing/current-later files. Previously completed file writes remain real. A write failure can be partial and is external. |
| B16 · inference.ts:346–396 | T · `inference.prompt.template`, Liquid reason | Inference. After preparation/files, before recording new prompt intent or start/resume. Saved task and supplied original fresh-session prompt bypass the renderer; retain existing resume-own/session guards. |
| B17 · inference-context.ts:13–17,42–70; inference.ts:397–443 | **Engine-owned `INTERNAL_ERROR`**, safe existing internal message. Only the two canonical-template rerenders qualify. | Inference, context-window callback already ran, before new turn. Ordinary pre-turn internal Resume true, subject to existing cancellation/timeout precedence. A controlled seam may be needed to exercise this branch. `contextWindow`/`fits` exceptions retain the existing harness mapping. |
| B18 · inference.ts:595–645,707–879 | T · `inference.output.schema.repair.prompt`, repair attempt, Liquid reason, `phase:"after-result"` and fixed received-result sentence | Inference. Last provider result observed, current task owns provenance. False, no new repair intent or contradictory uncertainty suffix. JSON serialization, cleanup and stronger evidence follow their own paths. |
| B19 · inference.ts:646–705,707–879; common.ts:225–311 | M · `inference.output.transforms`, operation index/kind, new inference-mapper cause, `phase:"after-result"` and fixed received-result sentence | Inference. Provider/repairs, possible transcript and structured coerce have acted. Parent thread patch still uncommitted. False. Actual last task retained even without a session ID. Artifact/schema/storage failures keep their established code and recovery. |
| B20 · engine/src/primitive-evaluator.ts:269–286,392–408 | Existing `EVALUATION_EXPRESSION_FAILED`, fixed message and false. Invalid route result remains `EVALUATION_INVALID_RESPONSE` | Decision. Existing distinct public primitive contract. Preserve pre/post abort checks and successful observation. No new provider or author metadata. |
| B21 · decision.ts:56–73 | T · `decision.instructions` or `decision.question`, Liquid reason | Decision. Before selected LLM/classifier provider. Preserve missing/invalid response and provider error rules. |
| B22 · decision.ts:15–32,56–73; common.ts:108–126 | E · `decision.context.messages.where`, item index and predicate reason | Decision. After instruction/question render, before provider. Context assembly and serialization remain external to predicate attribution. |
| B23 · wait.ts:24–33 | T · `wait.prompt`, Liquid reason | Wait input. Before first park. No wait identity, timer, wake or input event. Do not rerender on wake. |
| B24 · wait.ts:6–15,40–42 | T · `wait.timestamp`, Liquid reason or fixed “value must render to a timestamp” | Wait until. Before first park. Normalize existing raw rendered NaN diagnostic/default true to fixed cause/false. |
| B25 · engine/src/run-manager.ts:1647–1708; apps/api/src/plugins/errors.ts:192–194 | Existing signal request HTTP 400 `EXPRESSION_ERROR` from DomainError. Existing request copy/details, no new run failure | Signal request to a parked wait. Before signal/wake append; preserve wait, identity, retry/concurrency and status. No run-level recovery flag applies. |
| B26 · engine/src/run-manager.ts:2506,3004–3038,3338–3351; infrastructure/src/fs/workspace.ts:14–35, owned-resources.ts:92–124 | T · `settings.workingDirectory.template`, Liquid reason or fixed empty-path reason. At file-return delivery, existing `return.failed.error` receipt instead. | Script (workspace cwd), heartbeat script probe or inference. Invalid render reaches no mkdir/journal; retain prior inference task evidence when present. File-return local failure takes the existing channel catch; unexpected FS/write/receipt exceptions retain existing message/reconciliation. No new node failure for delivery. |

**Mutation operations covered by B14/B19.** Reuse the existing domain callback sites, with the new safe-cause inference mapper, at individual set-value template/expression, append/inject message template, truncate/drop/replace predicate, regex compilation, pointer/allowed-target/patch application and coerce repair-prompt/target write sites. A transform mapper recognizes only the source-owned domain errors from those calls. P01 keeps its own mapper and raw bounded cause text. Pure serialize-after-evaluation, engine clock/ID, structured completion, model selection, post-provider schema validation/final thread serialization have distinct origins. Keep `OUTPUT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`, `STRUCTURED_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT` and their established metadata when applicable. A previous repair completion is an actual provider action even if the failing operation never dispatched a main harness turn. [`packages/domain/src/mutations.ts:80–121,166–331`, `packages/engine/src/handlers/common.ts:208–311`]

**Parent/child and indexing.** Parent-owned mapping B11–B13 never uses the three reserved wrapper keys. Follow an actual failed-child link recursively for leaf inference evidence. Header/map order follows JavaScript own enumerable string-key iteration as specified in the plan.

**Existing precedents and adjacent surfaces.** P01 Mutate and P02 Exit already classify narrow source-owned causes and default these deterministic failures to false; preserve their existing public shape and tests, including `toJson` outside the Exit catch. A01 poll template/fireWhen/dedupe remains a pre-run trigger policy. A02 poll selector/key remains `POLL_ITEMS_INVALID`. A03 webhook/event dedupe remains a request-side 422. A04 preview remains a local response from a sample thread. No additional run error or migration for these four. [`handlers/mutate.ts:10–34`, `handlers/exit.ts:14–23`, `apps/api/src/triggers/poll.ts:143–269`, `packages/domain/src/poll-items.ts:71–93`, `apps/api/src/triggers/trigger-service.ts:463–475,617–627`, `apps/web/src/forms/preview.ts:19–27`]

**Cancellation and recovery across all rows.** Existing child cancellation, termination-unconfirmed veto, forced stop, run deadline and explicit cancellation precedence are determined in `packages/engine/src/run-manager.ts:2604–2704`; final patch/schema validation is separate at 2729–2745. An accepted submission cannot become a fresh resend. No new top-level failure event after cancellation or file-return finalization. Recorded script dispatch/completion, heartbeat beat and child terminal evidence continue to govern actual effects. Deliberate Replay remains subject to the current authoritative observation, reached-node and consent checks. Existing rows/events keep their original resumability and text.
